claims.text: The as-built additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an FCC matrix.
The as-built alloy exhibits AM-associated microsegregation and characteristic grain sizes.
Changing from a reducing or inert atmosphere to an oxidizing atmosphere while holding temperature, time, and stress constant will reveal the governing degradation behavior.
At approximately 800–900°C, an oxidizing atmosphere causes preferential oxidation along grain boundaries.
Chromium and titanium are preferentially involved in the proposed grain-boundary oxidation.
Oxidizing exposure produces Cr- or Ti-containing oxide precipitates along grain boundaries.
The proposed grain-boundary oxide precipitates are brittle.
Grain-boundary oxides reduce grain-boundary cohesion.
Reduced grain-boundary cohesion promotes premature crack initiation.
Brittle grain-boundary phases facilitate crack propagation under mechanical or thermal loading.
Oxidation-induced loss of grain-boundary cohesion can culminate in catastrophic failure.
Reducing conditions limit oxide formation relative to oxidizing conditions.
Limiting oxide formation under reducing conditions preserves ductility.
Oxidizing-atmosphere specimens will exhibit more grain-boundary oxidation than reducing- or inert-atmosphere controls.
Oxidizing-atmosphere specimens will exhibit lower fracture toughness than reducing- or inert-atmosphere controls.
Oxidizing-atmosphere specimens will exhibit more microcracking and a greater tendency toward catastrophic failure than reducing- or inert-atmosphere controls.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply over approximately 800–900°C at oxygen partial pressures sufficient to cause oxidation.
At lower temperatures or under different gas compositions, grain-boundary oxidation may cease to dominate degradation.
Residual stresses and AM-induced microstructural heterogeneities may also contribute to degradation.

The hypothesis is falsified if oxidizing specimens show no statistically significant, reproducible increase in grain-boundary oxidation accompanied by reduced mechanical performance relative to the reducing or inert controls.
